title: Request units, autoscale and the throttled request

videos.script: Cosmos DB bills its work in request units. {{ru}} Reading one item of one kilobyte, by its id and its partition key, is one unit. Everything else is measured against that. A bigger item, more indexed properties, a query that crosses partitions: each one costs more. {{factors}} You pay for those units in one of three ways. Reserve a fixed number every second. Let autoscale move between a tenth of a ceiling and the ceiling. Or pay per unit consumed, with serverless. {{modes}} A short program prices a month of Quitanda's orders all three ways. One hour of evening promotion decides which one wins. {{sizing}} When a second asks for more units than you reserved, the request is refused with a 429. The answer says how long to wait. {{throttle}} The library waits and retries for you, nine times, for thirty seconds at most. You will see where those numbers live and how to change them. {{retry}} The emulator charges one unit for everything and never refuses anything. So this lesson does the arithmetic by hand, and marks where the emulator's numbers stop meaning anything. {{emulator}}
